language.script_notes: German with umlauts (ä, ö, ü) and the ß letter; transit stops read 'Haltestelle'. One-way streets are marked 'EINBAHN' on red-and-white poles, with 'ANFANG' and 'ENDE' at the start and end. Vienna's street signs carry the district number at the top, low numbers near the center.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White bollard with a black cap, a red reflective rectangle on the front and a white reflector on the back; the black cap is one of the easiest Austrian tells, though Slovenia and Montenegro share black caps.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Slim white post with a black cap.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Utility poles may be painted red and white. Road signs often have grey borders and are held by metal clips. Commercial signboards have blue backgrounds, a contrast with the darker boards in Germany and Slovenia. Vienna's navy district-number street signs appear on almost every street.

architecture.roof_style: Steeply pitched gable roofs and wooden chalet-style roofs in the mountains; small onion-domed church spires across the countryside.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Baroque churches topped with onion domes in villages; timber Alpine chalets; grand Habsburg-era buildings and coffee houses in Vienna.

nature.vegetation: Alpine meadows, spruce and pine forest on the slopes, and farmland and vineyards in the east and Danube valley.
nature.terrain: Mountainous in the west and south, with the jagged peaks of the Alps visible from Innsbruck to Bregenz, opening into hills and the Danube plain in the east.
nature.climate_signature: Cool, snowy Alpine winters and mild green summers.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with black text and a blue EU strip on the left carrying 'A', with red-white-red bands along the top and bottom of the plate.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense coverage of roads including mountain passes.

confusion_set.shared_traits: German-speaking Alpine landscape, wooden chalets and tidy roads
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Austrian plates have an EU strip and red-white-red bands, whereas Swiss plates are fully white; the black-capped bollard with a dark red reflector is Austrian; 'ß' is used here where Swiss German uses 'ss'; no low-camera car blur.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same language, Alpine architecture in Bavaria, similar signs
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The black-capped bollard, blue commercial signs, 'EINBAHN' one-way markings and grey-bordered road signs are Austrian; German plates carry a city-code system.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Alpine landscape and a similar black-capped bollard style near the southern border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Slovenian signage and darker commercial boards; German-language signs and blue commercial boards are Austrian.
